skill.name: context-fundamentals
skill.description: Understand the components, mechanics, and constraints of context in agent systems. Use when designing agent architectures, debugging context-related failures, or optimizing context usage.
skill.summary: Design, evaluate, and optimize context for reliable AI agent systems.
skill.author: Asmayaseen

security_audit.summary: All eight static findings are false positives caused by headings, prose, and fenced Markdown examples; no shell execution or system reconnaissance is present. Two semantic concerns remain in example code: unrestricted file reads and summaries promoted to the system role. These patterns require safeguards before production reuse.

remediation.issue: ProgressiveDisclosureManager opens caller-provided paths without enforcing its configured base directory.
remediation.suggestion: Resolve each path against base_dir, reject paths outside that directory, and document that callers must not supply untrusted paths.

remediation.issue: The summary injection example assigns generated conversation summaries the system role.
remediation.suggestion: Store summaries as untrusted data in a dedicated message or structured field, and prevent summarized instructions from gaining system authority.

static_findings.snippet: Avoid arbitrary character limits that split mid-sentence or mid-concept.
The most effective agents employ hybrid strategies. Pre-load some context for speed (like CLAUDE.md

semantic_findings.description: ProgressiveDisclosureManager stores base_dir but opens caller-provided paths without resolving or restricting them. Untrusted paths could expose files outside the intended content directory.

content.value_statement: Agent context can become noisy, expensive, and unreliable as tasks grow. This skill explains context structure and provides utilities for budgeting, validation, truncation, and progressive loading.
actual_capabilities: Explains system prompts, tool definitions, retrieved documents, message history, and tool outputs.
Compares preloaded context with just-in-time retrieval and hybrid strategies.
Estimates text and message token usage with a documented character-based approximation.
Builds prioritized context sections within a configurable token limit.
Truncates message history while preserving the system prompt, an existing summary, and recent messages.
Checks context for empty sections, missing sections, excessive length, and duplicate content.
limitations: Token estimates use a rough four-characters-per-token approximation instead of model-specific tokenizers.
Text truncation splits on whitespace and does not preserve exact model token boundaries.
The utilities are demonstration code and require testing, error handling, and security hardening for production.
File-loading helpers accept direct paths and need containment controls before processing untrusted references.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent Context Architecture
use_cases.description: Define what an agent should preload, retrieve on demand, compact, and retain across a long workflow.

use_cases.title: Diagnose Context Failures
use_cases.description: Trace unreliable behavior to context volume, information position, stale history, or oversized tool outputs.

use_cases.title: Teach Context Engineering
use_cases.description: Introduce context components, attention constraints, progressive disclosure, and practical budgeting guidelines to a technical team.

prompt_templates.title: Map Context Components
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the five main context components for [agent]. Identify what should always load and what should load only when needed.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an agent design

prompt_templates.title: Create a Context Budget
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this context plan: [plan]. Estimate major token consumers, identify low-signal content, and propose a prioritized budget with compaction thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Context Degradation
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this agent failure: [symptoms and context trace]. Separate context quality, position, history, and tool-output causes, then recommend measurable tests.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Context System
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production context architecture for [workflow] using [model limits and tools]. Include retrieval, caching, truncation, summary trust boundaries, path controls, and degradation tests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert architecture planning with security constraints

output_examples.input: Plan context for a support agent that uses policies, account data, and long ticket histories.
output: Keep current policy and task constraints near the beginning.
Retrieve account records only for the active customer.
Compact resolved ticket details while retaining decisions and unresolved actions.

output_examples.input: Explain why an agent misses requirements in a very long prompt.
output_examples.output: The context may contain too much competing information or place key requirements in a weak attention position. Test a shorter prompt with requirements repeated near the end.

output_examples.input: Review a context plan that loads every reference document at startup.
output: Replace full startup loading with lightweight document identifiers and summaries.
Retrieve detailed sections only when the current task needs them.
Measure token use, retrieval accuracy, latency, and task quality before deployment.

best_practices: Keep the smallest high-signal context that supports the current decision.
Place critical instructions near the beginning or end and measure behavior under realistic context loads.
Treat retrieved content, tool output, and generated summaries as untrusted data with explicit authority boundaries.
anti_patterns: Do not preload every available document without evidence that the task needs it.
Do not rely on approximate token counts when enforcing a hard model limit.
Do not promote generated summaries or retrieved instructions to the system role.

faq.question: What does this skill teach?
faq.answer: It explains context components, attention constraints, progressive disclosure, token budgeting, message truncation, and validation for AI agent systems.

faq.question: Which tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Are the token estimates exact?
faq.answer: No. The included estimator uses a rough character ratio and recommends model-specific tokenizers for production measurements.

faq.question: Does the skill execute external commands?
faq.answer: No. The command alerts come from Markdown fences and static documentation examples, not executable shell calls.

faq.question: Are the Python utilities production ready?
faq.answer: No. They are demonstration utilities that need stronger path controls, model-aware tokenization, error handling, and dedicated tests.

faq.question: Does it prevent prompt injection?
faq.answer: No. It explains prompt structure but does not sanitize retrieved content or generated summaries. Production systems need explicit trust boundaries.
